header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood), Priya Singh (Atlas Payments - Platform Eng), Michael Lee (Atlas - CTO), Jared Wu (Atlas - Backend), Kara O'Neil (Atlas - Security)
Recording: yes
Location: Zoom
summary: AE + SE walked Atlas Payments through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, covering auth (API key vs. mTLS), env setup, example generate/chat/embeddings calls, and Console/Optimize highlights. Security questions around KMS, VPC/private deployments, and audit logs were raised; SE committed to share SOC2/architecture docs and run a small benchmark. Agreed next steps: share code snippets, security docs, and schedule dedicated-capacity deep dive.
transcript:
00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone - thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick walkthrough SDKs for python and TS, auth, env setup, and a couple quickstarts. 
00:18 Priya (Atlas): awesome, thanks. main goal for us is to get a poc integrated fast and validate latency/cost. we already have some inference on prem but want a simpler way to serve embeddings and chat.
00:32 Samira (SE): cool, quick heads up - we'll show hosted API first, then note how Dedicated/Private changes auth and networking. any blockers up front?
00:40 Michael (CTO): mostly data residency and key mgmt. we need KMS support and audit logs. also curious about client libs, how do we auth?
00:50 Alex: good call. for quickstarts you can auth with an API key in an env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY) for hosted. for Dedicated/Private you can use mTLS or integrate customer KMS; we'll share the spec.
01:05 Jared: is there a terraform module or CLI for the private deploy?
01:09 Diego (Redwood): we have a private deployment package + terraform references, yes. we'll link the repo.
01:18 Samira: jumping into code - python quickstart: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize..."}]) - simple. same pattern for TS: import {Redwood} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
01:42 Priya: nice. how about streaming? can we stream tokens?
01:45 Samira: yes - streaming supported via server-sent events in TS and an iterator in Python. we showed examples in the quickstart gist. note: streaming behavior is different if you enable continuous batching - small latency vs throughput tradeoff.
02:05 Kara (Security): on audit logs - retention and per-user token traces important for us. do you capture request/response or only metadata?
02:13 Alex: we capture full request metadata and can redact full responses depending on settings; audit logs available in the console and exportable to your SIEM. for private deploys you can keep logs in your VPC storage.
02:29 Samira: demo time - switching to a share screen, terminal: show project init. npm init -y; npm i @redwood/inference; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXX; node quickstart.js. here's the minimal chat example, small typos in comments in the gist but works.
03:05 (screen share) 
03:20 Samira: now embeddings quickstart - python snippet: client.embeddings.create(input=["invoice 12345 contents"], model='redwood-embed-1'); the response is a vector and id. store vectors in your DB. we recommend prefix caching for sessioned chat to reduce tokens.
03:50 Priya: what's prefix caching?
03:55 Samira: it caches previously seen prefixes/kvs for repeated contexts to avoid re-sending tokens to the model; reduces cost and latency for chat loops. available on runtime by default but controllable via the SDK options.
04:20 Michael: throughput - if we need 2k qps for embeddings, how do we size? Hosted vs Dedicated?
04:28 Diego: for that throughput we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools; we provide sizing guidance. for hosted we can run benchmarks but might hit rate limits, we can also set up burst windows. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet.
04:45 Jared: about quantized models and latency - do you automatically pick quantized variants?
04:49 Samira: runtime selects model variants/quantization friendly kernels based on config; you can pin model versions in the request. quantization helps cost but test quality regressions. Optimize suggests profiles per workload.
05:10 Priya: environment setup for CI - we want to run integration tests in CI without leaking keys. recommended approach?
05:16 Alex: use short-lived tokens or HashiCorp Vault/OIDC; we support ephemeral tokens via our token service and recommend injecting via CI secrets. we'll include example GH actions and Gitlab snippets.
05:30 Kara: encryption at rest - how do keys get rotated and are they customer-managed?
05:34 Alex: hosted supports Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS for enterprise tiers; keys can be rotated and we publish rotation events. for Private you always use customer-managed KMS.
05:50 Samira: switching back to code - quick TS example of streaming: client.chat.stream(...).on('data', chunk => { console.log(chunk.text) }) - small transcribe errors may appear in the example comments but functionality is correct.
06:20 Priya: any SDK differences between chat/generate/embeddings?
06:24 Samira: pattern is consistent: client.chat.*, client.generate.*, client.embeddings.*; request shapes vary but auth/transport and logging behave same.
06:40 Michael: integrability question - do you have official OpenTelemetry hooks?
06:44 Diego: yes we have tracing hooks and logging integrations; they send spans to your collector of choice. we'll share the quickstart for opentelemetry.
06:58 Jared: for TypeScript typings - do you ship types for response schemas?
07:02 Samira: yes - TS SDK is typed; python returns dicts but we have typed pydantic models in the sdk package if you'd like.
07:20 Priya: what about rate limits and throttling behavior?
07:24 Alex: per-account quotas and per-api-key rate limits; SDK handles 429s with exponential backoff. for Dedicated you can adjust quotas.
07:40 Kara: audit again - retention, SSO, RBAC - want a clear doc of permissions levels.
07:46 Alex: will send RBAC matrix and SSO/SAML setup steps.
07:55 Samira: quick note on Console and Optimize - Console gives token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards; Optimize will recommend batching, quantization and cache settings tuned to your workload. you can run evals tied to prompt suites.
08:12 Priya: can Optimize run on our data? we want recommendations based on our typical invoice prompts.
08:18 Samira: yes - you can run offline evals; for private deployments we can run Optimize in a VPC mode or provide guidance to run locally.
08:30 Alex: let's do a tiny live test - I'll run a Python snippet to call embeddings and then a chat.
08:35 (typing)
08:45 Alex: python -c "from redwood import RedwoodClient; import os; c=RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); print(c.embeddings.create(input=['a sample invoice']))" - response returned in 1.2s locally, vector length 1536.
09:05 Priya: that latency is great. was that with streaming or single call?
09:08 Alex: single call; streaming not used for embeddings.
09:12 Michael: curious about privacy - do responses persist on Redwood servers?
09:17 Alex: by default we persist metadata and can retain requests per your retention policy; for no-retention you can opt-out and set data retention to zero, or use Private deploy to keep everything inside your network.
09:34 Priya: any gotchas when moving from dev to prod?
09:38 Samira: watch for prompt token explosion, make use of prefix caching, tune batching and monitor latency SLOs. Optimize can generate a recommended batching config.
09:54 Jared: when you say "prefix caching" is that the KV cache we saw in the docs?
09:58 Samira: yes sometimes called KV cache; it's per-session caching of key-values for transformer states. works best for multi-turn chat.
10:12 Kara: if we require SOC2 Type II, is that supported?
10:15 Alex: yes, Redwood has SOC2; we'll share the report under NDA.
10:22 Michael: procurement - pricing model for dedicated? committed monthly seat or GPU pool?
10:27 Diego: committed GPU pool pricing with options for burst capacity and overage; we'll share a sample quote and pricing tiers.
10:40 Priya: custom models - can we bring our finetuned model?
10:44 Samira: for Private you can deploy your model; for hosted we support customer model hosting in Dedicated in some cases - we'll confirm for your model format.
10:56 (brief cross talk)
11:10 Alex: ok recap - we'll send code snippets (python + ts), security artifacts (SOC2, KMS doc), terraform references for private, a benchmark template, and schedule a dedicated deep dive.
11:25 Priya: great. one ask - can you also provide a small repo with CI examples for GH actions?
11:30 Alex: yes will include.
11:35 Michael: thanks all.
11:38 Alex: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts; expect email with links by end of week.
11:45 (meeting ends)
